title: Author plugin fixtures and the three-belt parity test
action: Per plan.md E3: the parity predecessor died with the Node runtime (R6) — author from zero, inside the declared cargo suite so commands.test runs it. New integration test file opencode_plugin_contracts.rs: (1) fixture tests that execute the real .opencode/plugins/bee-guard.ts under `node` (subprocess from the Rust test; skip-with-named-reason if node is absent) feeding recorded tool.execute.before payloads against a stub bee binary that can deny, allow, crash, and be absent — asserting throw-on-deny, allow passes args through, crash=>throw, missing-binary=>throw for every BLOCKING mapped row, and advisory rows never throw; (2) the three-belt parity test: derive the guard-rule inventory from the catalog of record (hook_manifests.rs rows / the hooks the CLI serves, see tests/hook_contracts.rs:37-47 — derived, never a hand list, per docs/knowledge/patterns/20260722-a-coverage-gate-derives-ground-truth-it-never-compares-two-hand-lists.md) and assert every blocking rule is exercised by BOTH a helper-level test and each runtime belt's fixture (claude hook fixtures exist in hook_contracts.rs; opencode rows point at the fixtures in (1); codex rows at its file-shipped hooks) — a rule missing a belt fails with a message naming rule and belt. Record the runner design and any skipped-environment behavior in discovery.md.

truths: The parity inventory is derived from the catalog of record, never a hand-authored list
Every blocking mapped row has crash=>deny and missing-binary=>deny fixtures
Advisory rows are asserted never to throw
The suite runs under commands.test (cargo), with any environment skip named in its output
